evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in the excavation"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was walking along a trench inspecting the trench box in the excavation when he tripped and fell toward the trench. The employee suffered amputations of his left index, middle, ring, and little fingers.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "inside a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was working inside a trench when a pipe fell onto his right lower leg, resulting in a fracture.

An employee was helping with an underground water line replacement. A sling that was connecting a road plate to an excavator released and the plate fell on the employee's big toe. The toe was medically amputated.

An employee was standing on a burial vault lid approximately 3 to 4 feet below grade hand-shoveling soil off the lid. An excavator was at rest on ground level accepting the shovels of soil. The excavator bucket inadvertently moved, causing the boom to swing. The excavator bucket then pinned the employee's hip to the wall of the grave, resulting in a fractured pelvis.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 651 (OIICS 2)
narrative: An employee was working in a 4-foot-deep trench. A clay section of the trench wall fell in and struck her back. She suffered fractured vertebrae.

The injured employee was helping two other employees replace the bucket attachment of an excavator with a ripper attachment. The injured employee's right hand was struck by the thumb accessory and crushed against the excavator's support arm.

An employee was leaf blowing to help clean the road. An excavator began backing up and caught the employee's foot, causing her to fall to the ground. The employee sustained the loss of a tooth, abrasions to the face and hand, and a cut to the foot.

An employee was fusing 10-inch black rubber utility pipes together using a pipe fusion machine and could not get the pipes to set correctly. The employee used a nylon strap attached to an excavator to lift one side of a pipe off a steel plate. As his hand was between two pipes, the pipes came back together, partially amputating two of his fingers.
An employee was driving an excavator that went off the road and tipped over. The employee was hospitalized with fractures and internal injuries. Their left arm was partially amputated.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 651 (OIICS 2)
narrative: An employee was doing electrical work in a trench when one of the trench walls caved in. The employee was struck by the soil and sustained fractures to their ribs and pelvis.

An employee was using an excavator on a barge to scoop and remove fertilizer product stored in the cargo area. As the employee was transporting the skid-steer by chains and hoisting equipment from the dock to the barge, the employee fell approximately 10 feet off the skid-steer bucket to the cargo hold area below. The employee suffered a concussion.
An employee's right middle finger was crushed by an excavator bucket, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was walking backward, cleaning a roadway with a flat shovel. A rubber-tracked excavator, also backing up, approached the employee. Its tracks caught the employee's pants, which caused the employee to fall forward. The machine then caught the edge of the employee's foot. The employee suffered bruising to both feet and an ankle, as well as a bone chip on the front of the right heel.

An employee and an excavator operator were investigating a potential hydraulic leak on one of the hoses on the arm of the machine. As the operator went to position the arm of the excavator for the employee to have a closer look, the employee's left leg was pinched between the excavator arm and a coil of steel. The employee's leg was broken.
An employee was stick welding on an excavator bucket that was being repaired when their shirt caught on fire, resulting in third-degree burns to their left armpit, inner arm, and ribcage.

An employee was working on an excavator track. He was heating a part when hardened grease particulate struck his face, causing his face to contact the bottom side of the moving track. The employee suffered injuries to his eye, nose, and cheek that included lacerations and multiple broken facial bones that required surgery.

The injured employee drove a dump truck to a worksite to unload a portion of rock. A mini excavator was parked and waiting on the shoulder of the road. When the injured employee exited the dump truck, the mini excavator rotated and the injured employee's middle finger was caught between the cab door of the excavator and the open door of the dump truck, resulting in a distal amputation of the third digit.

A picnic pavilion was being repaired. An employee was on the roof of the pavilion attaching an excavator boom. The boom moved unexpectedly and knocked the employee from the roof. The employee landed on the ground 10 feet below and suffered fractures.

An employee was wrapping a chain around a concrete manhole tube. An excavator, being used as a crane, started to lift the tube and cinched the chain. The employee's left middle finger was caught by the chain, which amputated the fingertip.

An employee was retrieving rigging straps to begin rigging a stack of wooden and concrete forms to be lifted via an excavator boom off a bridge deck. While retrieving the straps, he stepped between the stack of forms and the excavator boom. At this time, the excavator shifted, causing the boom to shift and strike him in the head and neck area. The employee suffered a nondisplaced fracture to the jaw, a fracture on the right facial orbital area, and a neck laceration on his left side.

An employee was using a chipping hammer to remove asphalt from around a manhole cover. The hammer got stuck and an excavator operator attempted to remove the hammer using an excavator bucket. The employee reached down to help when the hammer engaged, causing the bucket to jump and pin the employee's left ring finger between the bucket tooth and the hammer. The employee suffered a fingertip amputation.

An employee was climbing up the side of a wall at a construction site when his right hand fingers were hit by an excavator boom, resulting in a laceration to the ring finger and fractures to the middle and little fingers.

An employee was replacing a heating unit on an excavator. As they stepped off the excavator, the employee lost footing and fell striking their head on the concrete. The employee lost consciousness and was hospitalized for a brain bleed that required surgery.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "edge of a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was standing at the edge of a trench while handing shoring materials to two employees in the trench below. The concrete beneath where the employee was standing gave way causing the employee to fall approximately 8 feet into the trench. The employee was hospitalized with contusions and lacerations to the neck, back, and shoulder.
An employee was backing up a skid steer from a fuel tank after refueling and struck a parked excavator, resulting in an avulsion injury to their upper right leg.
An employee was standing on the track of the excavator refueling it. He slipped off the track and fell approximately three feet to the ground, resulting in fractures to his hip and coccyx bone.

The injured employee was spotting for the operator of an mini-excavator. The mini-excavator was about to begin digging when the bucket came down and landed on the injured employee's foot. The employee was hospitalized with a broken foot.

A mechanic was using a hammer to seat a bucket tooth onto an excavator bucket on the jobsite. A chunk of metal flew off the bucket tooth and went under the mechanic's safety glasses and impaled his eye.

An excavator was being used as a crane to perform rigging operation. An employee was guiding additional drainage into place when their right index finger was caught between the wire rope and the load resulting in medical amputation at the first knuckle.
An employee was walking near an excavator when the excavator struck them. They were hospitalized with broken bones in their foot.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "edge of an approximately 4-foot trench"; "trench"

An employee was was descending from an excavator. The employee's hands slipped and they jumped, landing on their left foot and suffering a compound fracture to the lower left leg.

A crew of three employees was pulling electric cable through 1,200 feet of HDPE conduit. The rope pulling the cable was attached to the bucket of an excavator. The excavator was pulling it back in stages, between which the rope would be untied so the truck could move forward and the rope could be re-tied. When one of the employees untied the rope, the tension in it caused it to catch his right hand and lacerate his middle finger. He was hospitalized.

An employee was performing the final alignment of an MSE panel installation while an excavator was parked perpendicular to the MSE wall. When it broke, the force of the excavator bucket pushed the employee through the safety barrier causing him to fall to the ground. This resulted in facial injuries and a fractured arm.

An employee was fueling an excavator from the fuel tank in the bed of the truck while standing on the bumper of the truck. The plastic on the bumper broke, causing the employee to fall to the ground and resulting in a fractured right femur just below the joint.
An employee was struck by a reversing excavator resulting in broken bones in the right leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was pouring concrete forms into a trench when another employee threw a board to him, causing him to fall approximately three feet to the dirt floor of the trench. The employee sustained a fractured shoulder and four or five broken ribs.

An employee had been operating an excavator from the safety platform and was putting tree limbs onto the belt of a horizontal grinding machine. A limb got stuck in the grinder. Employees raised the anvil and the limb was removed. When the anvil was being lowered back down, the employee's right foot got crushed between the top of the anvil guard and the grinder frame. They sustained two toe fractures and a partial amputation to one toe.
An employee was walking and waiting to pull an axel out of a trach compactor machine when they were struck in the right foot by an excavator bucket, resulting in three fractures to the foot.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was in a 13-foot trench busting concrete with a sledgehammer and a drill to fit a pipe in a junction box. The employee suffered a puncture wound and fractures to his face below the right eye.

An employee was handling metal sheet piles during installation. The piles were suspended by an excavator and guided into position by hand. The employee's left hand was caught between the suspended sheet and the installed sheet adjacent to it while a pile was lowered into position. The employee sustained a laceration to the tip of the ring finger and two broken bones and a laceration to their left pinky.
An employee was paving a road when an excavator backed over his right foot. He suffered a broken toe.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "edge of a six-foot-deep excavation"; "excavation"
narrative: An employee was working along the edge of a six-foot-deep excavation when he slipped and fell in the opening. The employee's leg was caught between an existing pipe and the wall of the excavation causing fractures that required hospitalization.

An employee was adjusting a septic tank that was being lowered into the ground by an excavator using a cable. The employee's hand was on the septic tank when the cable slipped off the excavator and caught their left thumb, amputating it at the first knuckle.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was placing a securing pin into a trench box. The pin slipped, pinching his right gloved hand in the cylinder. His thumb was broken and he was hospitalized.
An employee was changing out attachments to an excavator boom and connecting hydraulic lines when the thumb piece on the boom engaged, resulting in a fracture to their left foot.
An employee was walking beside an excavator as it was moving forward when they were struck by the excavator, resulting in a fractured right leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was operating a demolition saw to cut into a 6-inch ductile water main pipe for a new water connection in a trench. The pipe shifted, causing the saw to kick back and strike the employee, resulting in a 6-inch laceration to their right arm bicep/shoulder.
An employee was securing an excavator to a trailer for transport when they tripped and fell off the trailer. The employee sustained a broken heel and was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: On May 27, 2024, an employee was checking the depth of a trench when they slipped and fell into the trench. They sustained an avulsion injury to their lower left leg from a mini skid steer with a trencher attachment that was in operation.

An employee was operating an excavator to free a grinding machine that had become mired in mud. As the excavator exerted force, the pin shackle being utilized to connect the excavator to the grinding machine with a tow strap failed and snapped back, striking the employee in the excavator in the upper left chest. The employee sustained a puncture wound to his upper left shoulder, rendering him unconscious. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was sitting on a form board of a house when the teeth of a mini-excavator struck their shin, causing a fractured leg.
An employee was assisting with rigging at the ground level when they became caught between a moving excavator and a piece of shoring. They sustained fractured ribs and a collapsed lung.

An employee was raking loam along a drainage ditch prior to grass seeding. They stepped out of the ditch and were struck by an excavator that was backing up. The employee sustained fractures to their leg and pelvis, and severe skin and muscle damage to their left leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in the trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was in the trench box in an excavation when an 8" ductile iron pipe was lowered into the trench and pinned the employee's left leg against the trench box, fracturing it.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the shallow excavation"; "excavation"
narrative: An employee (driver) was operating a backhoe digging footing inside the building. The backhoe slipped into the shallow excavation and the employee sustained broken ribs.

On June 12, 2024, an employee was hand grading behind an excavator with rubber tracks and tripped and fell while the machine was backing up. The excavator ran over the employee's right leg resulting in a broken ankle, cracked pelvis and a fractured left arm.

An employee was clearing debris and preparing an area for the installation of railing. The hydraulics on the excavator failed, causing the guardrailing to fall. He was sitting on the ground when a piece of railing fell and struck his back, causing fractures to his vertebrae.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "inside a trench"; "trench"

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)

evidence: OSHA source code 611
narrative: On July 5, 2024, an employee was serving a search warrant when they fell into a ditch while in pursuit of a suspect. The employee sustained a torn patellar tendon.
An employee was removing a pin from an excavator bucket when a pry bar popped and struck them in the jaw, fracturing it. The employee was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "excavation caved"; "excavation"
narrative: An employee was spotting for an excavator that was pulling an old pipe from the ground. The wall of an adjacent excavation caved in and caused the excavator to tip into it. An employee was welding a steel pipe when they were struck in the back by an excavator bucket, resulting in fractures to their pelvis and right tibia.

evidence: OSHA source code 611
narrative: An employee stepped out of a delivery van he had just parked, fell into a ditch at the edge of the yard, and suffered a broken ankle.
An employee was utilizing an excavator to move piping material when it tipped over. The employee suffered a left wrist fracture, a laceration, and a contusion to back of head and was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was working in a trench in 93-95 degree weather. He became light-headed and was taken to the hospital with heat stroke.

narrative: Employees were testing and repairing a sewer line while in a trench that was approximately 3.5 feet deep. Employee 1 was treated but not hospitalized. Employee 2 was hospitalized with a fractured pelvis and injury to the abdominal area.

Employees were pushing culverts into place with an excavator. A pin slipped, catching the injured employee's left hand in a pinch point. The left middle and ring fingers were medically amputated at the hospital.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was installing pipe in a trench when he felt cramping in his legs and stomach. The employee sustained a heat-related illness.

An employee was strapping down a mini excavator. While walking down the ramp they slipped and their right foot became caught under the blade of the mini excavator. The blade lowered and crushed their foot, fracturing it.

On August 5, 2024, an employee was fueling an excavator. He was walking on the excavator tracks to turn the fuel pump on. While walking back down the excavator track, he tripped and fell striking his head on the excavator bucket and causing his safety glasses to become lodged under his right eye. The employee was hospitalized for lacerations to the back of his right eyeball.

An employee was helping to change a hose on an excavator. He was in the raised bucket of a powered industrial vehicle (PIV) when his 15-inch adjustable wrench slipped off a nut. He lost his balance and fell about 8 feet to the ground. The employee sustained injuries to their neck and back, a laceration to his head, and fractured ribs. A fall arrest system was not used at the time of the fall.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the area and stepped into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: Employee 1 removed the grate over a drain trench in front of the fryers to remove a clog. Employee 2 was walking back into the area and stepped into the trench with his right foot, causing him to lose his balance. He used his right arm to stop his fall and his arm went into the fryer, resulting in a burn on his right forearm.

Employees had used an excavator to pull a hydrovac unit that had high-centered. The injured employee then went under the hydrovac to disconnect the tow line. The hydrovac lurched forward and ran over the employee's leg. The employee was hospitalized with a degloving injury to skin on their thigh.
An employee was giving a hand signal to an excavator operator. The excavator's bucket jumped horizontally and struck the employee's foot, causing multiple fractures.

An employee was filling an excavator bucket with water. When the bucket activated to dump the water, the bucket crushed the employee's right leg. The employee sustained a fractured leg that required surgery.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was installing piping in a trench that was 6-7 feet deep when the trench collapsed and soil pinned them up to their waist. The employee sustained a bruised bladder and fractures to their pelvis and sacrum.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "edge of a 12' benched trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was standing on the edge of a 12' benched trench when the side collapsed and he fell into the trench. His legs were buried and he sustained a fractured pelvis and fractures to his left femur, tibia, and fibula.

evidence: OSHA source code 611
narrative: An employee was performing horticulture-related work inside of an attraction when he stepped backward into a trough in the concrete floor and fell backward sustaining a back injury.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: A crew was installing 48" x 6" concrete storm drainpipe. The pipe was lowered into the trench and placed against the other pipe so that a track excavator front head arm can connect the two pipes. The injured employee was inside the pipe standing in front of the excavator head arm when the arm lifted and struck the employee on the side of their body causing a contusion with a rib fracture.
An employee was installing an electrical box when they became pinned between the bucket of an excavator and the electrical fiber box. The employee sustained a laceration to their left inner leg.
An employee was measuring a wire mesh sheet behind a mini excavator when the excavator reversed and ran over the employee's leg, resulting in a leg fracture that required hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was guiding a concrete lid that was suspended from the boom of an excavator by chain straps and pins. A pin failed, causing the lid to fall approximately 1 foot and land on the employee's left foot. The employee was hospitalized with a broken toe and a crush injury to the upper left portion of the foot.

An employee was greasing a pipe at the bottom of the hill to prepare it to be placed inside another PVC pipe. An excavator was working at the top of the hill about 10 feet away from a pile of 30-inch PVC pipes placed behind a berm. The vibration caused the pipes to dislodge from the berm and a pipe rolled down the 8-10-foot slope. The employee's right leg was caught between the fixed pipe he was working on and the pipe that rolled down the slope and fractured.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "bottom of the trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was cleaning shavings from a skin mill machine. He stepped backward into a hole in the grate and was injured by the floor/bottom of the trench. The employee sustained a laceration to his left forearm and a right tibial plateau fracture.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a ground cable trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was on the back of a pickup truck helping to unspool wire from a large wire reel. The employee was exiting the truck, tripped over the elevated lift on the back of the truck and fell. As he was falling he jumped to avoid a partially lowered liftgate. His right foot landed on the asphalt and his left foot landed in a ground cable trench, resulting in multiple fractures to his left leg.

An employee was unloading a mini-excavator from a trailer. The mini-excavator tipped over and fell off the trailer with the employee inside. His right foot was pinned under the machine and sustained an injury.
An employee was setting a concrete pipe in the street when the excavator shifted causing the pipe setting apparatus to shift, resulting in the amputation of the employee's left thumb tip.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was receiving red boards for shoring in a trench. As a board was being handed down, it slipped and pinched the employee's left ring finger between the board and the shoring, resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee was performing housekeeping tasks when they were struck on the right shoulder by a mini excavator bucket, causing the employee to fall forward and strike the asphalt in front of him. The employed sustained a frontal lobe brain bleed, fractures to their right shoulder, orbital bone, and nose, as well as a forehead laceration.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)

The employee was hospitalized with 12 fractured ribs and 4 fractured vertebrae in his lower back.

An employee was using an excavator (with hydraulic shears mounted on it) to move, shear, and cut old steel trusses. He set a truss on the ground in front of him and began adjusting the position of the excavator. The truss rolled into the cab of the excavator and struck his right leg below the knee. He suffered a broken tibia and fibula as well as a wound to the lower leg.
An employee was operating an excavator on top of an unprocessed pile of construction and demolition waste. The machine tipped over and the employee suffered a back injury.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "out of a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was being lifted out of a trench using an excavator. The excavator's bucket closed, causing broken bones in his forearm.

On October 24, 2024, an employee was hooking a claw to an excavator bucket via a chain on the end of an excavator. Their left middle finger was caught between the chain and the bucket as the excavator arm was lifted, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was installing a pin to secure an auger attachment to an excavator. As the excavator positioned the Kelly bar, the employee's left hand was caught between the first and second stage of the Kelly bar friction plates (flanges) connected to the auger. The employee sustained fractures to their index finger, middle finger, and thumb.

An employee was performing quality assurance at an on-ramp when a mini-excavator with rubber tires rolled over his feet, resulting in fractures to both feet, a fractured right ankle, and a laceration on his right foot.
An employee was connecting a 4-way chain to an excavator when they became caught between the excavator and a concrete structure. The employee sustained broken ribs.

An employee assisted with lifting a sand/salt spreader out of a truck onto a steel stand for work to be done on the sander chain. The employee went to unhook the chain from the excavator bucket. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to their vertebrae, ribs, and pelvis.

An employee was guiding a pump that was being lifted by an excavator when the pump swung and pinched the employee's left hand between the pump and the excavator, resulting in crush injuries to the hand and fingers.
An employee was injured inside a car wash tunnel that was being built when he stepped on a trench grate and his leg fell through, causing a fracture to his left leg.

On December 2, 2024, at approximately 9:00 AM, an employee was removing the drive head from an excavator. The drive head shifted and pinched their right hand against the excavator. The employee was hospitalized with crush injuries to the hand.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was installing a pipe while approximately 16 feet deep in a trench box. Soil became loose and fell onto the pipe, causing the pipe to move and pin the employee against the trench box wall. The employee suffered abdominal injuries and was hospitalized.

An employee was conducting repairs on an excavator engine compartment while standing on top of it. The employee stepped on the removed engine door cover and slipped and fell approximately 7 feet to the ground, fracturing their left hip and femur.

A crew was moving a radial stacker. One of them was moving an electric cable when an excavator struck his abdomen with its teeth. He was hospitalized with a puncture wound to the left side of the abdomen that resulted in damage to muscle tissue.

An employee was loading an excavator onto a flatbed. After loading the heavy equipment onto the flatbed, the employee fell off the flatbed and sustained a fractured bone in his leg and a dislocated shoulder.

An employee and truck driver were delivering three concrete box culverts on a flatbed truck. evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)

An employee was operating an excavator at the bottom of a hill. A haul truck dumped processed slag at the top of the hill, causing hot dust to travel to the bottom of the hill and enter the excavator. The employee sustained second- and third-degree burns to their hands and wrists.

evidence: OSHA source code 611

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"

An employee was using the 4-foot ladder of an excavator to replace a hydraulic element on the excavator. They were climbing down the ladder when they fell 4 feet onto their side on the ground, resulting in a broken shoulder.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"

An employee was working in a ditch while a mini excavator was digging in front of them. Teeth on the excavator bucket struck the employee's left foot, resulting in a fracture.

An employee was preparing to unload a barge. He was on the deck of a barge as it was being discharged and was struck by an excavator bucket, which knocked him into a structure on the barge, resulting in a fractured right arm.
An employee was performing groundwork when the tracks of an excavator ran over his foot, resulting in crush injuries that required hospitalization.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "inside a trench"; "trench"

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into an excavation"; "excavation"

narrative: An employee was in a trench, welding/installing a new pipe that was being held up using an excavator. The excavator arm rotated, and the employee was pinned between the pipe and the trench box. The employee suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung.
An employee was using an excavator to place debris bags in a dumpster when the bucket came off and rolled onto their right leg. The employee sustained a lower body injury and was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "inside a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was inside a trench to remove a piece of asphalt from the top of a pipe. A piece of asphalt and part of the trench wall fell and struck the employee, resulting in a dislocated left shoulder and a facial contusion; the employee also experienced tingling in their left hand.

An employee was loading an excavator onto a trailer. While the employee was tying the chains together, the crane tightened up and pulled his hand into the machine, lacerating his left index finger. The employee sustained a partial amputation of the finger.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: The injured employee was assisting with the placement of two trench boxes or installing sewer pipe in a trench box when their right hand was contacted by the excavator attachment and the spool. The employee's hand and fingers were crushed.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was working in a trench and exiting the trench using a ladder when the trench collapsed on him. He fell from the ladder and suffered a fractured left leg.

A crew was preparing a 20-foot section of 12-inch high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipe to be swung into a welder using an excavator, where it would be welded onto a longer run of pipe. One employee was facing the longer pipe in the welder while the 20-foot section was being rigged. The 20-foot section moved and struck the employee's left knee. The employee's left leg was broken below the knee.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was standing next to a trench box waiting to hook up a steel plate for removal. The plate shifted and the employee fell into the trench, resulting in broken ribs, a bruised lung, and multiple contusions.

On 3/27/2025, at approximately 8:00 AM, an employee was dismounting a mobile excavator after fueling it with diesel. He lost his balance, slipped, and fell approximately three feet, striking his rib cage against a metal step on the excavator. The employee sustained multiple left rib fractures and a partially collapsed left lung.

Employees were loading an excavator onto a flatbed truck. The injured employee was holding a piece of chain attached to the excavator and was guiding the machine operator when the excavator bucket lowered onto their right hand. The employee sustained amputations to their right middle, ring, and little fingers.

An employee was performing a pipe count while a pipeline contractor was unloading steel pipe at a staging yard. The contractor was preparing to set a pipe segment (12 diameter) on the top row of a pyramid-shaped stack using an excavator. The pipe stack shifted as the contractor began to position the pipe, and the bottom piece (42 feet long and 2,083 pounds) rolled onto the injured employee s lower left leg, trapping the employee underneath it. The employee was hospitalized with a compound fracture of his tibia and fibula and he required surgery.

An employee was changing a manual steel thumb on an excavator. When the thumb was disconnected, he lost his balance and fell from the excavator bucket he had been standing on. The thumb then pinned his left foot and knee, causing injuries to the foot and the knee that resulted in swelling and ligament damage.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the excavation"; "excavation"
narrative: Two employees were standing next to a 2 1/2-foot-deep excavation when its edge collapsed. Both employees fell into the excavation; one landed on the other's upward-pointing knee and suffered broken ribs and a lung injury.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into a trench"; "trench"

An employee was setting a portion of trench drain by hand. The piece was approximately 30 inches long and weighed 50 pounds. The employee lost his grip and his little finger was pinched between the piece and another piece that was already set in place, resulting in a fingertip amputation including bone.
An employee was attaching a bucket onto a mini excavator when the bucket slipped and crushed both of their hands, resulting in a fractured right hand and partial amputations of two fingertips.
On April 18, 2025, an employee was entering an excavator cabin when they fell to the ground and broke a hip.

An employee was walking when they were struck by an excavator and their lower legs were caught between the excavator track and a crane mat. The employee's legs were crushed and their lower leg was amputated.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into an open excavation"; "excavation"
narrative: A traffic control employee fell 30 inches into an open excavation, resulting in a fractured tibia and fibula.

An employee was rigging a portable welding machine to the lifting hook of an excavator. Their right hand became caught between the excavator bucket and the welding machine. The employee sustained a laceration to their hand and a fracture/dislocation to their middle finger.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: On May 1, 2025, an employee was cutting a pipe while working inside a trench that was 20' long x 3.5' deep x 4.5' wide. A shaft of dirt fell onto the employee's leg. The employee sustained an injury to their anterior tibial artery.
An employee was struck by an excavator bucket and caught between the bucket and a stone pile. The employee sustained a fractured left arm and lacerations.
An employee was loading an excavator onto a trailer. He jumped off the excavator and suffered a spine fracture. He was hospitalized.

An employee was helping to set concrete traffic barriers by guiding a barrier clamp weighing approximately 600 pounds that was connected to an excavator. The employee guided the clamp down on top of the barrier successfully, which then disengaged the locking pin and allowed the clamp to scissor and grab the barrier to raise it again. As the excavator operator hoisted the barrier clamp to move the segment of barrier, the employee's left ring fingertip got caught in the scissor area of the barrier clamp, resulting in a transphalangeal fingertip amputation.

An employee was replacing a hydraulic cylinder on a mini-excavator. The employee was positioning the machine while it was in a trailer when their right leg became pinned between a track and the trailer, resulting in severe lacerations to the lower leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: On May 19, 2025, multiple employees were installing a 42-inch storm pipe in a trench that was 17 feet deep and 15 feet wide. The excavator operator was signaled to scoop soil from inside the trench to continue laying the pipe. As the operator went to remove the soil, the injured employee was pinned by the excavator bucket against the pipe, resulting in hospitalization for a fractured scapula and sternum.

An employee was using an excavator to unload concrete traffic barriers. The excavator swung, tipped over an existing barrier, and fell into a ravine/wetland. The employee sustained a fractured left shin requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was installing gas lines when a tracked excavator drove over the employee's right foot. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to their tibia and fibula.

An employee was emptying bulk bags/sacks of lime into a lime pit. A sack fell into the lime pit. The employee was directing an excavator to pick it up when the excavator struck the employee, fracturing their left ankle against a concrete barrier.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was climbing a ladder to get out of a trench when the trench collapsed. The employee's leg was trapped in soil and their ankle was fractured.
An employee was working on a mini-excavator with a stuck ignition. He was shutting down the mini-excavator engine when he suffered an amputation of the left middle fingertip.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was walking across a board that had been placed across a trench that was about 2-3 feet deep. The employee fell into the trench and contacted the dirt edge of the trench. The employee sustained a contusion to his arm and four fractured ribs.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: On June 20, 2025, an employee was in a trench box, observing while an S-fitting was being removed from a 48-inch pipe with an excavator. The pipe shifted and struck the employee in the head. The employee sustained head trauma to the left temple and was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was digging out and cleaning a 10-foot deep trench he'd just finished excavating. He climbed into the trench to conduct a sewer line repair and the trench collapsed on top of him. As a result of the cave-in, another employee jumped into the trench to save him, causing further injury. The employee was severely bruised and was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in the trenches"; "trenches"
narrative: A temporary employee was installing conduit pipe in the trenches and started to feel ill, weak, and had cramps. The employee sustained heat stress.

Employees were moving an electrical utility line and removing an electrical box. As they were preparing to lift a 4-inch conduit using an excavator, the conduit swung and struck the injured employee, causing lacerations, fracturing their left arm, and bruising their ribs. They were hospitalized.
An employee was walking behind an excavator during roadside construction. The excavator reversed and ran over the employee's left foot, breaking it.
Employees were using an excavator to move an I-beam as part of pile driving work. When the I-beam was lifted, it struck an employee and fractured his left leg in three places below the knee.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: Employees were working to apply sealant to a customer's leaking foundation. The injured employee was digging out dirt and passing it to another worker. The hole that was being dug collapsed and the injured employee became trapped in dirt/mud from the waist down. The employee sustained a fractured pelvis.

An employee had been spotting for a mini-excavator. The employee was working to relocate a water pump to give the mini-excavator an adequate area for the spoil pile. The employee retrieved the water pump located beside a 24'' metal manhole cover. As he started walking, his right foot stepped on the edge of the manhole cover and his right leg went into the opening up to his knee. His left leg and foot remained on the ground and twisted as he lost balance and fell to the ground. The employee sustained a closed dislocation of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the left foot and required surgery.

The injured employee was assisting with hitching a trailer to a truck. The employee was working to engage the lunette ring on the trailer with the pintle hook on the truck. A mini-excavator began driving onto the rear of the trailer. The added weight caused the rear of the trailer to lower and the front to rise, creating a pinch point between the trailer and the truck. The employee s left thumb was caught in the latch mechanism of the pintle hook. The thumb tip was partially amputated and required surgery.

An excavator operator and the injured employee were exchanging a hand tool on a utility right of way. After the tool exchange the excavator moved forward and the tracks ran over the big toe of the injured employee's right foot. The toe was crushed, resulting in amputation of the tip.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: On July 30, 2025, at approximately 8:30 AM, an employee was installing a storm drain pipe in a trench that was approximately 14 feet deep. While working near the edge of the trench, the employee exited the trench box. A section of the trench wall collapsed, striking the employee and causing him to fall into an adjacent manhole box within the trench. The employee sustained a dislocated shoulder and a fractured femur.

An employee swapped the bucket on his excavator and began digging when the bucket fell off and into an embankment. The injured employee was checking the grade in the embankment and was struck by the excavator bucket, fracturing his right tibia, fibula, and ankle.
An employee was using an angle grinder to grind a pin on a quick coupler for an excavator. The grinding wheel failed, resulting in a cheek laceration, fractured orbital bone, and a ruptured eyeball.
An employee was rigging a pipe to an excavator bucket so it could be lifted. The employee suffered a fingertip amputation, caused by the rigging and the bucket.
An employee's right hand was broken after being struck by an excavator that was being moved.

An employee was walking next to an excavator on a road. The excavator ran over his foot and fractured it. It also caused injury to the muscles in his leg that required his leg be amputated below the knee.

An employee was working on an excavator's tracks. He was swinging a sledgehammer to finish pushing a metal tractor pin into the track links. A hammer-blow caused a piece of the pin to fly off, ricochet, and embed itself in his buttock. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
A flagger was walking behind a mini-excavator. The excavator backed into him and fractured his heels, his left ankle, and his left wrist, as well as injuring a tendon in his left thumb.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was digging in an excavation less than five feet deep to locate existing underground utilities. Side wall shear occurred in the excavation and the employee was struck by loose pieces of asphalt pavement and soil in the lower half of their body. The employee sustained a fractured pelvis.

The employee climbed down inside the unguarded trench to get measurements and do leveling for the stabilizing sand. The employee started to prepare the sand so they could lay the pipe. An excavator put some sand into the trench. Dirt then fell on him resulting in fractures to an arm and a leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: A crew was installing 8-inch polyvinyl chloride (PVC) waterline in a trench. An employee was soaping a joint to insert the spigot end of a pipe into the previously laid joint when the joint was pushed together. The employee's left ring and little fingers were pinched between the two pipes. The ring finger was injured and the little fingertip was amputated.

Pile-driving operations were being conducted when a steel I-beam broke loose and fell horizontally. The beam hit an excavator and rolled into an employee who was standing nearby, signaling commands to the excavator operator. The employee's leg was fractured and nearly severed.

An employee was assisting with temporary traffic control setup when they were struck on the right foot by the outrigger of an excavator. The employee sustained a degloving injury to the top joint (knuckle) of the fourth toe.

An employee was operating a mini excavator, using the boom to move a barrel of rebar. The excavator rolled over while on uneven terrain, and the employee was struck by the interior components of the cab during the rollover. The employee suffered four cracked ribs, a broken scapula, and a collapsed lung.
An employee was stacking trimmed branches. A branch shifted and hit the door of the excavator equipment. The employee's finger was caught in the door and fractured. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was directing a mini excavator operator to unload materials. The bucket of the mini excavator struck the employee, resulting in a fractured right leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "inside a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was working inside a trench box in an excavation, putting gravel under a pipe. An excavator dropped gravel from its bucket into the trench. When the excavator began to curl out its bucket, it pinned the employee's right leg between the bucket and a spreader bar, causing two lacerations (one below the knee and one above). The employee was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into the trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was installing network infrastructure at a client's distribution center. He was transporting a box measuring approximately 23 inches by 12 inches to a truck yard and walking along a narrow path adjacent to a trench that measured approximately 5.5 to 6 feet deep, 10 to 12 feet long, and 18 to 24 inches wide. Gravel on the path shifted beneath the employee's foot, causing him to lose balance and fall into the trench. He landed on his left side and struck a 4-inch PVC conduit pipe located at the bottom of the trench. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to his fourth, fifth, and sixth ribs on the left side.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was working in a trench that was 3.5 feet deep when soil fell and hit them, resulting in an injury to their pelvis. The employee was hospitalized.

narrative: An employee was backfilling a trench using a concrete auger. When the trench transitioned to a different depth, the auger articulated and the front-right tire lodged itself in the deeper portion of the trench, causing the auger to tilt to the right into the ditch. As the machine was teetering toward the ditch, multiple employees brought a mini excavator to hook onto the cement auger to shift it upright. As the auger was pulled back out of the ditch, it articulated to the left and caught the injured employee's leg between the bucket on the excavator and the side of the auger. The employee suffered a fracture and injured muscle tissue in his leg.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "in a trench"; "trench"
narrative: An employee was helping the operator of a 360-degree excavator to install a storm drain box in a trench that was approximately 2.5 feet deep. While the operator was repositioning the bedding box to be reloaded with bedding material, it became disconnected from the excavator and fell to the ground. The momentum carried it into the trench, where it struck the employee and knocked him to the ground. The employee suffered injuries including a broken arm, broken collarbone, and a lacerated left arm, resulting in hospitalization.

An employee was standing on the outside edge of a hopper barge while watching a skid steer push ore for an excavator (with a clamshell bucket) to unload. The excavator was on a work barge. The bucket of the excavator struck the employee and caused a near-amputation of their right arm and fractures of the ulna and radius of the left arm. The right arm required surgery.

The injured employee was standing by the controls for the electric spud system on the barge, preparing to raise the spuds. Meanwhile, an excavator was moving a mat on the deck. As the excavator swung from port to starboard, it's counterweight struck the injured employee s shoulder, causing them to lose balance and fall against the spud controls. The employee sustained bruises and contusions to their right shoulder and chest.

On September 26, 2025, an employee was performing maintenance on an excavator when a bale of rubber fell from an adjacent rack and struck him. The employee sustained multiple fractures to his pelvic area.
An employee was working from the elevated bucket of an excavator when they fell between two tanks and landed on the ground. The employee sustained a fractured leg.

On September 19, 2025, an employee was exiting an excavator when his foot slipped off the rubber track. He suffered an abrasion and contusion to the right shin as it slid down the track. He was hospitalized.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: "into a 1-foot-deep trench"; "trench"
narrative: A backhoe tractor was moving gravel into a 1-foot-deep trench, and an employee was helping spread the gravel. He was hospitalized, having suffered an abdominal injury that caused internal bleeding.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was standing in an excavation, about 12 feet deep, to check a natural gas pipeline for leaks. The excavation's sides sloughed, and the employee was buried up to the waist. The employee suffered a broken left lower leg.

An excavator bucket was being removed. An employee was pulling a snap ring to remove a pin and lost his grip. The high-tension snap ring recoiled and his left middle fingertip was amputated by the snap ring.

The injured employee was operating a boring machine. Another employee was operating an excavator. The excavator bucket came in contact with the injured employee, resulting in a pelvic fracture when they were pinned against the boring machine. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was operating a mini excavator and had the bucket down with one side of the track elevated for the injured employee to loosen dirt on the track. While the excavator operator was spinning the track to remove dirt, the injured employee went to grab a rock and their hand was pulled into and ran through a sprocket. The employee sustained fractures and lacerations to their right hand.
An employee was carrying a piece of 4-inch steel pipe when he tripped on a trench cover and fell, suffering a laceration to the left thumb. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

evidence: OSHA source code 611

He fell backward into the ditch, landing on asphalt on his right shoulder and then striking his head. The employee lost consciousness and was hospitalized due to a head laceration and a broken vein in the right shoulder that required surgery.

evidence: trenching or excavation operation: OSHA event code 632 (OIICS 3)
narrative: An employee was using a hammer to break away old existing sewer pipe from underneath a building. A section of dirt/rock fell from the side of the underground tunnel wall onto the employee's legs. The employee sustained two broken legs.
